facts.claim: Some dunes produce sustained low sound during avalanches.
facts.sensitivity: Do not conflate Great Sand Dunes footage with Eureka location or claim a settled microscopic mechanism.

facts.claim: The NPS recording is from Great Sand Dunes National Park.
facts.sensitivity: Do not conflate Great Sand Dunes footage with Eureka location or claim a settled microscopic mechanism.

facts.claim: At Eureka Dunes, dry sand can boom; damp sand does not.
facts.sensitivity: Do not conflate Great Sand Dunes footage with Eureka location or claim a settled microscopic mechanism.

facts.claim: The sound can resemble a low organ note or distant airplane.
facts.sensitivity: Do not conflate Great Sand Dunes footage with Eureka location or claim a settled microscopic mechanism.

facts.claim: Research has proposed different mechanisms for sustaining dune sound.
facts.sensitivity: Do not conflate Great Sand Dunes footage with Eureka location or claim a settled microscopic mechanism.

facts.claim: Relative motion of grains during avalanches is linked to dune sound; synchronization is an influential explanation.
facts.sensitivity: Clapping is an original analogy, not an observed microscopic experiment. Motion shown slow, not at audible frequency.

facts.claim: Suitable singing-dune sand produced sound in laboratory avalanches in a hard-bottom channel.
facts.sensitivity: Only under tested conditions; do not claim ordinary sand can always sing.

facts.claim: Sorting the mixed-size sand into a narrower grain-size range produced a more defined note.
facts.sensitivity: Sieve selects existing grains; it does not resize them. No numerical spectrum claimed.

facts.claim: Field studies proposed layered-dune waveguides, while other experiments emphasize flowing grains.
facts.sensitivity: Competing interpretations; no claim of complete resolution.

facts.claim: Sound in air propagates as pressure disturbances while air particles oscillate locally.
facts.sensitivity: Diagram is slow and symbolic, not a measured molecular simulation.

facts.claim: Silo studies measured discharge-driven vibration and sound linked to stick-slip wall friction in tall narrow silos.
facts.sensitivity: Related engineering domain; not claimed identical to dune acoustics.

facts.claim: A flexible bag of granular material can conform to an object and become more rigid under vacuum to grip it.
facts.sensitivity: Related granular physics, not a direct invention from singing-dune research.

facts.claim: The 2015 field study distinguished brief burps and sustained booming and reported 70–105 Hz peaks at investigated sites.
facts.sensitivity: Do not universalize frequency range or present waveguide interpretation as the only explanation.

facts.claim: Pitch, loudness and spectral concentration are different sound properties.
facts.sensitivity: Selecting grain sizes does not resize grains or simply imply increased loudness.
